name: usb.ids
desc: Repository of vendor, device, subsystem and device class IDs used in USB devices
why: A data repository of USB vendor IDs; a door into USB enumeration, but the entry itself is just a database.

brief.what_it_is: usb.ids is a public database of identifiers used by USB hardware: vendors, devices, subsystems, and device classes. It is published as a plain-text usb.ids file, with daily snapshots also offered gzip- and bzip2-compressed. Tools such as the USB Utilities read that file and turn numeric IDs into human-readable names. Input comes from volunteer submissions through a web interface or as patches emailed to a mail robot, and the output is the generated usb.ids file. The brew package has no executables, so it is a data file rather than a command.
brief.why_it_exists: The page says the repository exists so programs can show full human-readable names instead of cryptic numeric codes. It is maintained by volunteers who add unidentified devices and fix existing entries.
brief.how_it_works: Volunteers submit new entries or corrections through the web interface or by emailing patches of the usb.ids file to a mail robot. Updates that change existing entries should include a discussion comment explaining the reason. The site generates a snapshot of the database every day and offers it as usb.ids, usb.ids.gz, or usb.ids.bz2.
brief.install_notes: No install steps, runtime, account, or configuration were described on the homepage. Using the data means downloading a snapshot of usb.ids, and a consuming tool such as the USB Utilities reads it. Accounts are only needed to submit data through the web interface.
brief.standout: It is a dataset rather than a program, and the page is explicit about its licensing: the contents and generated files can be used under either GPL v2 or later or the 3-clause BSD License. The site also shares its web code with the PCI ID repository, and the page asks that PCI ID maintainers not be contacted for help with this site.
brief.status: maintained. The homepage says the database is maintained by Stephen J. Gowdy and that daily snapshots are generated. No specific date of the latest update appears on the page, and I did not check the repository's commit history.
brief.caveats: The data is only as accurate as its volunteer contributors, and the page asks submitters to avoid vague entries. The homepage itself has no commands, install steps, or version information. I read only the homepage and did not follow the linked source code or the help pages.
quotes: This is a public repository of all known ID's used in USB devices: ID's of vendors, devices, subsystems and device classes.
to display full human-readable names instead of cryptic numeric codes.
please submit only accurate information – descriptions like "unknown modem device" are hardly useful for anybody.
fetch_log: http://www.linux-usb.org/usb-ids.html - fetched successfully; returned the USB ID Repository page text, which was complete enough that no further links were followed.
